newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open weaker after surprise rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open weaker after surprise rate hike.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in active trade on Thursday after the Bank of Canada surprised many in the market by hiking short-term interest rates for the first time in more than two years, analysts said.

"Obviously the short end is going to be most impacted by a rate rise. The long end in Canada is keeping pace with the U.S. Both markets are down on the day," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with financial analysis firm Technical Data.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.48 to C$115.79 to yield 6.762 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.75 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to one basis point from a negative spread of one basis point at Wednesday's close.
The Bank of Canada raised its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.5 percent by intervening in the money market.

The move raised the central bank's target range for the call loan or overnight lending rate to 3.0-3.5 from 2.75-3.25 percent. It was the first time the central bank hiked Canadian short-term interest rates since February 1995.
"Just as we were starting to talk about how soon the bank would come in, boom, they came in. I think it still caught some speculative accounts off guard," said Technical Data's Hall.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.42 to C$107.73 to yield 6.194 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which fell 4/32 to yield 6.46 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 27 basis points from 30 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.10 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.11 percent.
